name: Autoimmune Gastritis

criteria.description: Presence of anti-parietal cell antibodies and/or anti-intrinsic factor antibodies
Gastric mucosal biopsy showing chronic atrophic gastritis predominantly affecting the corpus and fundus with lymphocytic infiltration
Evidence of pernicious anemia with vitamin B12 deficiency and elevated methylmalonic acid/homocysteine
Elevated serum gastrin levels due to achlorhydria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anti-parietal cell or anti-intrinsic factor antibodies plus histological confirmation of atrophic gastritis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Vitamin B12 deficiency and pernicious anemia support diagnosis but are not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Loss of gastric acid secretion due to parietal cell destruction
Macrocytic anemia caused by vitamin B12 deficiency

common.notes: Due to anemia and vitamin B12 deficiency
Inflammation of the tongue associated with B12 deficiency
Mild upper abdominal pain or discomfort
Unintentional weight loss in chronic disease

occasional.notes: Peripheral neuropathy due to B12 deficiency

rare.notes: Cognitive impairment, depression related to B12 deficiency

laboratory: Macrocytic anemia with low vitamin B12
imaging: Endoscopic evidence of gastric mucosal atrophy
Possible gastric neuroendocrine tumors on imaging
other: Histopathology showing chronic atrophic gastritis with lymphocytic infiltration
Achlorhydria confirmed by gastric pH testing

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly affects antrum rather than corpus
Less commonly associated with pernicious anemia
History of NSAID or bile reflux exposure
Histology shows reactive gastropathy rather than lymphocytic infiltration

redFlags: Severe macrocytic anemia with neurological deficits
Rapid weight loss or persistent vomiting
Evidence of gastric neoplasia or carcinoid tumor
references: Neumann WL, et al. Autoimmune atrophic gastritis—pathogenesis, pathology and management. Nat Rev Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2013.
Tack GJ, et al. Autoimmune gastritis: current perspectives. Clin Exp Gastroenterol. 2015.
Kaptan K, et al. Helicobacter pylori-negative autoimmune gastritis: a distinct entity? World J Gastroenterol. 2006.
